description: Figure 8 is a line plot titled “Sᵣ ratio ablation study,” illustrating the trade-off between model perplexity and GPU memory usage as the proportion of recent sequence (Sᵣ) is varied. The x-axis, labeled “Recent Sequence Ratio (%)”, ranges from 0 to 100 in increments of 20. The left y-axis, labeled “Perplexity”, spans from 4.2 to 4.7, while the right y-axis, labeled “GPU Mem. Ratio (%)”, ranges from 40 to 100. Four lines are plotted: “Perplexity” (orange, solid line with circle markers) starts at ~4.6 at 0% Sᵣ, dips to a trough of ~4.3 at 40–60%, then rises slightly to ~4.4 at 100%. “Full Cache PPL” (red, dashed line) is a horizontal line at ~4.35, representing the baseline perplexity of the full cache method. “GPU Mem. Ratio” (blue, solid line with circle markers) increases steadily from ~42% at 0% Sᵣ to ~98% at 100%. “Full Cache GPU Mem.” (blue, dashed line) is a horizontal line at 100%, indicating the baseline GPU memory usage of the full cache method. The plot demonstrates that increasing the recent sequence ratio reduces GPU memory usage but introduces a non-monotonic effect on perplexity, with optimal performance (lowest perplexity) occurring at intermediate Sᵣ ratios (40–60%).
